data.why: The tool is a single self-contained HTML file with no external data dependencies; a scientist defines blocks and scenarios directly in the UI at session start, so no example files need to be supplied.

goals: Configure a new field session by defining measurement scenarios (e.g. soil depths or GPS placement conditions) and spatial blocks (e.g. fields or plots)
Generate a randomized complete block design (RCBD) schedule from the defined scenarios and blocks
Log GPS receiver power-on time, RTK fix time, and time-to-first-fix (TTFF) for each receiver used
Record weather conditions for the session, either via device GPS, place-name search, or manual entry
Run the guided point-by-point collection workflow with start/stop timers, flagging and re-collecting points as needed
Export the completed session as CSV or JSON and verify the exported columns match the documented schema

review.summary: The tree matches the README's stated purpose (a session notebook with a seeded RCBD schedule, receiver TTFF, weather, timed points, redos and export), and every screen I opened shows what its node claims. Before filing it needs the export-schema check marked as done from the README, a note that redoing a point wipes its original times, the receiver-fix rule for starting collection, and a few corrections to the feature wording.
